english.title: Disclose information received from HMRC otherwise than for the purpose of the livestock export regulations
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the prior consent of the Commissioners for His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs, disclosed information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), received from the Commissioners relating to a person whose identity was specified in, or could be deduced from, the disclosure otherwise than for the purposes of enabling an enforcement authority to carry out its functions in relation to the export of relevant livestock
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 19 and 15(a) of the Animal Welfare (Livestock Exports) Enforcement Regulations 2024.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location disclosed information received from Commissioners for HMRC where
the information related to a person whose identity was specified in the disclosure / could be deduced from the disclosure OR
disclosure was not for a purpose of enabling an enforcement authority to carry out any function conferred on it by the Animal Welfare (Livestock Exports) Enforcement Regulations 2024 or Animal Welfare (Livestock Exports) Act 2024 OR
the Commissioners had not given their consent prior to disclosure

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) It is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that that person reasonably believed that the disclosure was lawful; or the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(ii) See regulation 14 for offences by bodies corporate.
(iii) See regulation 16 for the power of prosecution afforded to a local authority.
